headline: Computational methods infer cell dynamics and missing states from single-cell snapshots
label: Computational Single Cell Inference Methods
summary: Recent preprints and papers recover temporal dynamics, fate bias, and spatial expression from static or sparse single-cell and spatial measurements.
synthesis: The common thread is recovering quantities that single-cell and spatial measurements do not directly observe, including temporal dynamics, division-resolved flows, fate bias, and signaling history, from static snapshots or sparse readouts. Several items model trajectories: SUDO solves simulation-free unbalanced dynamic optimal transport with general convex growth penalties, AnnFlux learns object-conditioned neural SDE drift fields for perturbation trajectories, DRIFT infers division-resolved flows by solving a population-balance equation, and DiffusionOT combines optimal transport with neural ODEs across multi-timepoint data. Ageas instead infers fate bias without time labels. Spatial items reconstruct missing information: Emerge recovers transcriptome-scale expression from targeted panels, CellART segments cells and annotates types, and PhenoMapR projects bulk phenotype signatures onto single-cell data. The dominant thread is inference under incomplete observation, though methodological scope and modality vary across items.
